name: Benign Breast Diseases, Fibroadenoma, Duct Ectasia, and Breast Abscess

reference.source: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22nd ed / Royal College of Radiologists Guidelines
clinicalPearls: Triple assessment of any breast lump combines clinical breast examination, radiological imaging, and core needle biopsy
Fibroadenoma is the most common benign breast neoplasm in women under 35, presenting as a highly mobile, discrete rubbery mass
Phyllodes tumors display stromal hypercellularity with leaf-like architecture and require wide local excision with a 1 cm margin
Intraductal papilloma is the most frequent cause of unilateral spontaneous serosanguinous or bloody single-duct nipple discharge
Lactational breast abscess is managed primarily with ultrasound-guided needle aspiration and continued breastfeeding from the unaffected breast
reference.pathophysiology: Benign breast disorders arise from aberrations of normal lobular and ductal development, involution, and cyclic hormonal stimulation (ANDI framework). Fibroadenomas represent localized hyperplastic proliferations of both intralobular stroma and epithelial elements. Periductal mastitis involves squamous metaplasia of lactiferous ductal lining with keratin plugging, duct dilation, rupture, and secondary bacterial infection (Staphylococcus aureus and anaerobes), frequently associated with cigarette smoking and recurrent subareolar fistulae.
additionalDifferentials: Benign fibroadenoma versus malignant phyllodes tumor with aggressive stromal overgrowth
Fat necrosis with traumatic oil cyst mimicking scirrhous invasive ductal carcinoma
Periductal mastitis with subareolar abscess versus inflammatory breast carcinoma
Mammary duct ectasia with green nipple discharge versus intraductal papillary neoplasm
additionalInvestigations: Breast ultrasonography in women under 30 years and diagnostic digital mammography in women 30 years or older
Core needle biopsy (14-gauge) to obtain tissue architecture and distinguish in situ lesions
Microdochectomy with cannulation of the single discharging duct for definitive histopathology
Ultrasound-guided aspiration of purulent breast collections with Gram stain and culture
